# Bartib

Bartib is an easy to use time tracking tool for the command line. It saves a log of all tracked activities as a plaintext file and allows you to create flexible reports.

Usage examples

Start a new activity:

  bartib start -d "Description of the activity" -p "Project Name"

Stop the running activity:

  bartib stop

Continue the most recent activity:

  bartib continue

List today's activities:

  bartib list --today

Report for today:

  bartib report --today

Configuration

Bartib records activities in a plaintext log file. You can either pass the file explicitly with the -f/--file option, or set the BARTIB_FILE environment variable to point to your log file. Example:

  export BARTIB_FILE="/home/username/activities.bartib"

If the file does not exist, Bartib will create it when you start tracking.

Installation

Download a prebuilt executable from the project's releases and place it in a directory on your PATH (for example: ~/bin). Bartib may also be available through your distribution's package manager.

Autocompletion

Completion scripts for shells may be provided in the repository's misc/ directory. Source the appropriate script for your shell to enable completion of project and task names.

License

This project is provided under the terms of the LICENSE file in this repository.

_bartib_tasks() {
    local -a _tasks=($(bartib last | head -n -1 | awk 'BEGIN { a="" } NR > 2 {for (i=2; i <= NF - 1; i++) { if (i != 2) { a=a" "$i; } else { a=$i } } gsub("[\[\]]", "", $1); printf("%s[%s]\n", $1, a)}' | tr '\n' ' '))

    _values "TASK" ${_tasks[@]}
}

_bartib_projects() {
    local -a _projects=($(bartib projects --no-quotes | sort | tr '\n' ' '))

    _values "PROJECTS" ${_projects[@]}
}

_bartib() {
    typeset -A opt_args
    local context state line
    local current_context="${curcontext}"

    _arguments -C \
        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
        '(-v --version)'{-v,--version}'[Prints version information]' \
        '-f[the file in which bartib tracks all the activities]:FILE:_files' \
        '1:bartib commands:->commands' \
        '*:: :->command_arguments'

    case $state in
        commands)
            local commands
            commands=(
                'cancel:cancels all currently running activities',
                'change:changes the current activity',
                'check:checks file and reports parsing errors',
                'continue:continues a previous activity',
                'current:lists all currently running activities',
                'edit:opens the activity log in an editor',
                'help:Prints this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)',
                'last:displays the descriptions and projects of recent activities',
                'list:list recent activities',
                'projects:list all projects',
                'report:reports duration of tracked activities',
                'sanity:checks sanity of bartib log',
                'search:search for existing descriptions and projects',
                'start:starts a new activity',
                'status:shows current status and time reports for today, current week, and current month',

function __fish_complete_bartib_descriptions
    set -l output (bartib last -n 100 2>/dev/null)

    set -l description_match (string match -r '(\\e\[4mDescription.*)\\e\[4mProject.*' -g $output)
    set -l description_length (math (string length $description_match) - 8)
    string replace -r (echo "\[(\d)\] ([[:ascii:]]{0,$description_length}).*") '$2' (string match -r '\[\d\].*' $output)
end

# Bartib

Bartib is an easy to use time tracking tool for the command line. It saves a log of all tracked activities as a plaintext file and allows you to create flexible reports.

Usage examples

Start a new activity:

  bartib start -d "Description of the activity" -p "Project Name"

Stop the running activity:

  bartib stop

Continue the most recent activity:

  bartib continue

List today's activities:

  bartib list --today

Report for today:

  bartib report --today

Configuration

Bartib records activities in a plaintext log file. You can either pass the file explicitly with the -f/--file option, or set the BARTIB_FILE environment variable to point to your log file. Example:

  export BARTIB_FILE="/home/username/activities.bartib"

If the file does not exist, Bartib will create it when you start tracking.

Installation

Download a prebuilt executable from the project's releases and place it in a directory on your PATH (for example: ~/bin). Bartib may also be available through your distribution's package manager.

Autocompletion

Completion scripts for shells may be provided in the repository's misc/ directory. Source the appropriate script for your shell to enable completion of project and task names.

License

def parse_round_str(round_str):
    # Parses duration like "15m" or "4h"
    # Returns timedelta or (None, reason)
    round_str = round_str.strip()
    m = re.fullmatch(r"(\d+)([mh])", round_str)
    if not m:
        return None
    val = int(m.group(1))
    unit = m.group(2)
    if unit == "m":
        return datetime.timedelta(minutes=val)
    else:
        return datetime.timedelta(hours=val)

def round_datetime(dt, round_delta):
    # Round dt to nearest round_delta
    # round_delta is timedelta (minutes or hours)
    # We need to round to nearest multiple since midnight? Or since epoch?
    # For simplicity, round time of day to nearest multiple of round_delta?
    # But for 1h rounding, 09:30 rounds to 10:00 (as observed). For 15m rounding, 09:07->09:00, 09:08->09:15.
    # So we round the datetime to nearest multiple of round_delta from midnight? Let's think.
    # For 15m, intervals at 00:00, 00:15, etc. So 09:07 rounds to 09:00, 09:08 to 09:15. That matches rounding to nearest 15m since midnight.
    # For 1h, intervals at 00:00,01:00,... 09:30 rounds to 10:00 (as observed). Yes.
    # Need to handle date as well? If rounding crosses midnight, date should change? Possibly. For simplicity, compute seconds since midnight, add half, floor.
    # But for multi-day? Rounding should affect only time? For 1h rounding, if time is 23:40, rounding to nearest hour would be 00:00 next day? Might need to handle date increment.
    # We'll implement: compute timestamp, round to nearest round_delta seconds.

    # round_delta seconds
    delta_seconds = int(round_delta.total_seconds())
    # For rounding, we need reference at midnight of that day? Or epoch? Since we want intervals aligned to midnight, we should compute seconds since midnight.
    # Then round that.
    midnight = dt.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0)
    secs_since_midnight = (dt - midnight).total_seconds()
    # nearest
    remainder = secs_since_midnight % delta_seconds
    if remainder*2 < delta_seconds:
        # round down
        rounded_secs = secs_since_midnight - remainder
    else:
        rounded_secs = secs_since_midnight + (delta_seconds - remainder)
    # Handle overflow to next day
    rounded_dt = midnight + datetime.timedelta(seconds=rounded_secs)
    return rounded_dt

def format_duration(delta_seconds):
    # delta_seconds may be negative? But we handle.
    # Returns string like "<1m", "01m", "1h 00m"
    total_seconds = int(delta_seconds)
    if total_seconds < 60:
        return "<1m"
    total_minutes = total_seconds // 60
    hours = total_minutes // 60
    minutes = total_minutes % 60
    if hours == 0:
        return f"{minutes:02d}m"
    else:
        return f"{hours}h {minutes:02d}m"

def read_file(filepath):
    activities = []
    errors = []
    if not os.path.exists(filepath):
        return None, None, f"Could not read from file: {filepath}"
    try:
        with open(filepath, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    except Exception as e:
        return None, None, f"Could not read from file: {filepath}\n\nCaused by:\n    {e}"
    for idx, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        # line includes \n
        line_no_nl = line.rstrip("\n")
        # Preserve raw_line as line (with newline? We store without newline for reconstruction)
        parsed = parse_activity_line(line_no_nl, idx)
        if parsed['valid']:
            activities.append(parsed)
        else:
            errors.append(parsed)
            activities.append(parsed)  # keep invalid as well in list for file rewriting? We'll keep separate
    # Actually we need list of all entries (valid and invalid) in order
    # We'll return list of entries where each entry is parsed dict, and errors list is subset of invalid
    # For simplicity, return full list
    return activities, errors, None

    # For invalid, write raw_line + "\n"
    # For valid that are unchanged stopped, write as per preservation rules: datetime_raw lstrip, project_raw preserved, description_raw rstrip? Actually description_raw_rstrip = description_raw.rstrip() ? But need to preserve leading spaces
    # Let's implement as per our earlier deduction
    with open(filepath, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for e in entries:
            if not e['valid']:
                # invalid: write raw_line as is + "\n" (original raw_line may have been without newline, so add newline)
                # raw_line is line without newline, so we need to ensure we write it as original? Original may have had no newline at EOF? We'll just write raw_line + "\n"
                f.write(e['raw_line'] + "\n")
            else:
                # valid
                if 'write_as' in e:
                    # special handling for modified entries
                    # write_as indicates how to write
                    # For running->stopped trimmed, we have start, end, project, description trimmed
                    # For new running, start, project_raw_new, description_raw_new
                    # We'll handle via explicit keys
                    if e['write_as'] == 'stopped_trimmed':
                        start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

                        f.write(f"{start_str} - {end_str} | {proj_esc} | {desc_esc}\n")
                    elif e['write_as'] == 'running_new':
                        start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                        proj_esc = escape_str(e['project_raw_input'])
                        desc_esc = escape_str(e['description_raw_input'])
                        f.write(f"{start_str} | {proj_esc} | {desc_esc}\n")
                    elif e['write_as'] == 'running_preserve_changed':
                        # change command with new values preserving raw input spaces
                        start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                        proj_esc = escape_str(e['project_raw_input'])
                        desc_esc = escape_str(e['description_raw_input'])
                        f.write(f"{start_str} | {proj_esc} | {desc_esc}\n")
                    else:
                        # fallback
                        pass
                else:
                    # unchanged stopped: preserve
                    # datetime_raw lstrip
                    dt_raw = e['datetime_raw'].lstrip()
                    proj_raw = e['project_raw']
                    desc_raw = e['description_raw']
                    # desc_raw rstrip trailing spaces (but keep leading)

                    desc_rstrip = desc_raw.rstrip(" \t")

    from_filter = None
    to_filter = None

    if hasattr(args, 'date') and args.date:

        if df is not None:
            date_filter = df

    if hasattr(args, 'from_date') and args.from_date:
        df = parse_date_with_warning(args.from_date, "--from")
        if df is not None:
            from_filter = df

    if hasattr(args, 'to_date') and args.to_date:
        df = parse_date_with_warning(args.to_date, "--to")
        if df is not None:
            to_filter = df

    # Flags
    filter_today = getattr(args, 'today', False)
    filter_yesterday = getattr(args, 'yesterday', False)
    filter_current_week = getattr(args, 'current_week', False)
    filter_last_week = getattr(args, 'last_week', False)

    filtered = valid_sorted

    if filter_today:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() == today]
    if filter_yesterday:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() == yesterday]
    if filter_current_week:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if monday_current <= a['start'].date() <= sunday_current]
    if filter_last_week:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if monday_last <= a['start'].date() <= sunday_last]
    if date_filter:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() == date_filter]
    if from_filter:

    if to_filter:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() <= to_filter]
    if hasattr(args, 'project') and args.project:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['project'] == args.project]

    return filtered

def apply_rounding(activities, round_arg, warnings):
    if not round_arg:
        return activities, None
    round_delta = parse_round_str(round_arg)
    if round_delta is None:
        print(f'Can not parse "{round_arg}" as duration. Argument for --round is ignored')
        return activities, None
    # Round each activity's start and end (if end exists, else now)
    # For running activities, end is None, so we round start and also effective end (now) for duration calculation, but we should not modify now? We'll round start and end for display purposes only, not change actual stored.
    # So we need to return new list with rounded start/end for display
    rounded = []
    for a in activities:
        new_a = a.copy()
        new_a['original_start'] = a['start']
        new_a['original_end'] = a['end']
        new_a['start'] = round_datetime(a['start'], round_delta)
        if a['end']:
            new_a['end'] = round_datetime(a['end'], round_delta)
        else:
            # for running, end is now, rounded?
            now = get_now()
            new_a['end'] = round_datetime(now, round_delta)
        rounded.append(new_a)
    return rounded, round_delta

def compute_duration(activity, now=None, rounded=False):
    # activity has start and end (end may be None meaning running)
    # If running, end = now
    if now is None:
        now = get_now()
    start = activity['start']
    end = activity['end'] if activity['end'] else now
    # If rounded, we already rounded start and end
    delta = end - start
    return delta.total_seconds()

def format_duration_for_display(seconds):
    return format_duration(seconds)

    # Ignore parsing errors? Sanity should check valid activities

    for a in valid_sorted:
        if a['end'] and a['end'] < a['start']:
            issues.append(f"Activity has negative duration\n{a['description']} (Started: {a['start'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}, Ended: {a['end'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')}, Line: {a['line_num']})\n")

    # Check overlapping: If an activity starts before previous ends

        for iss in issues:

    # Find running activities
    valid = [a for a in activities_all if a['valid']]

    # We'll build list of entries in original order, but with running that are stopped modified

    for entry in activities_all:

                # running -> will be stopped at start_time
                # Create new stopped entry from this running
                # Use trimmed project/description (as observed)
                # The stopped entry's start is original start, end is start_time
                stopped_entry = {
                    'valid': True,

                    'line_num': entry['line_num'],

                    'end': start_time,
                    'project': entry['project'], # trimmed already
                    'description': entry['description'],
                    'project_raw': entry['project_raw'],
                    'description_raw': entry['description_raw'],
                    'datetime_raw': entry['datetime_raw'],
                    'is_running': False,
                    'write_as': 'stopped_trimmed',
                }

                print(f"Stopped activity: \"{entry['description']}\" ({entry['project']}) started at {entry['start'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')} ({format_duration_for_display((start_time - entry['start']).total_seconds())})")
            else:
                # stopped remains, preserve with our preservation rules
                # We'll keep entry as is, but for writing we use special handling that preserves raw
                # For unchanged stopped, we want to write as preserved: we will keep original raw fields
                # So we keep entry unchanged, but mark for preservation

    # We need to handle preservation of old stopped: our write_file currently handles valid unchanged as preserved, but we changed running to stopped_trimmed entries which will be written as stopped_trimmed
    # For unchanged stopped entries, we need to ensure write_file preserves as per rules
    # Let's implement write_file here directly

                'error_msg': f"could not parse activity (Line: {line_num})",
                'line_content': raw_line
            }
    else:
        # No dash, try single datetime
        single_strict = r"^\s*(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2})\s+(\d{1,2}):(\d{2})\s*$"
        m_single = re.match(single_strict, dt_str)
        if m_single:
            try:
                date_str = m_single.group(1)
                h = int(m_single.group(2))
                m_ = int(m_single.group(3))
                dt = datetime.datetime.strptime(f"{date_str} {h:02d}:{m_:02d}", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                proj_unesc = unescape_str(project_raw)
                desc_unesc = unescape_str(description_raw)
                return {
                    'valid': True,
                    'raw_line': raw_line,
                    'line_num': line_num,
                    'start': dt,
                    'end': None,
                    'project': proj_unesc.strip(),
                    'description': desc_unesc.strip(),
                    'project_raw': project_raw,
                    'description_raw': description_raw,
                    'datetime_raw': datetime_raw,
                    'is_running': True,
                }
            except:
                return {
                    'valid': False,
                    'raw_line': raw_line,
                    'line_num': line_num,
                    'error_type': 'date',
                    'error_msg': f"could not parse date or time of activity (Line: {line_num})",
                    'line_content': raw_line
                }
        # If it looks like date time but invalid, date error
        if re.match(r"^\s*\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\s+\d{1,2}:\d{2}\s*$", dt_str):
            return {
                'valid': False,
                'raw_line': raw_line,
                'line_num': line_num,
                'error_type': 'date',
                'error_msg': f"could not parse date or time of activity (Line: {line_num})",
                'line_content': raw_line
            }
        # Else activity error
        return {
            'valid': False,
            'raw_line': raw_line,
            'line_num': line_num,
            'error_type': 'activity',
            'error_msg': f"could not parse activity (Line: {line_num})",
            'line_content': raw_line
        }

def read_file(filepath):
    activities = []
    errors = []
    if not os.path.exists(filepath):
        return None, None, f"Could not read from file: {filepath}"
    try:
        with open(filepath, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    except Exception as e:
        return None, None, f"Could not read from file: {filepath}\n\nCaused by:\n    {e}"
    for idx, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        # line includes \n
        line_no_nl = line.rstrip("\n")
        # Preserve raw_line as line (with newline? We store without newline for reconstruction)
        parsed = parse_activity_line(line_no_nl, idx)
        if parsed['valid']:
            activities.append(parsed)
        else:
            errors.append(parsed)
            activities.append(parsed)  # keep invalid as well in list for file rewriting? We'll keep separate
    # Actually we need list of all entries (valid and invalid) in order
    # We'll return list of entries where each entry is parsed dict, and errors list is subset of invalid
    # For simplicity, return full list
    return activities, errors, None

def write_file(filepath, entries):
    # entries: list of dicts, where each dict may be valid or invalid, and may have been modified
    # For invalid, write raw_line + "\n"
    # For valid that are unchanged stopped, write as per preservation rules: datetime_raw lstrip, project_raw preserved, description_raw rstrip? Actually description_raw_rstrip = description_raw.rstrip() ? But need to preserve leading spaces
    # Let's implement as per our earlier deduction
    with open(filepath, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for e in entries:
            if not e['valid']:
                # invalid: write raw_line as is + "\n" (original raw_line may have been without newline, so add newline)
                # raw_line is line without newline, so we need to ensure we write it as original? Original may have had no newline at EOF? We'll just write raw_line + "\n"
                f.write(e['raw_line'] + "\n")
            else:
                # valid
                if 'write_as' in e:
                    # special handling for modified entries
                    # write_as indicates how to write
                    # For running->stopped trimmed, we have start, end, project, description trimmed
                    # For new running, start, project_raw_new, description_raw_new
                    # We'll handle via explicit keys
                    if e['write_as'] == 'stopped_trimmed':
                        start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                        end_str = e['end'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                        proj_esc = escape_str(e['project'])
                        desc_esc = escape_str(e['description'])
                        f.write(f"{start_str} - {end_str} | {proj_esc} | {desc_esc}\n")
                    elif e['write_as'] == 'running_new':
                        start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                        proj_esc = escape_str(e['project_raw_input'])
                        desc_esc = escape_str(e['description_raw_input'])
                        f.write(f"{start_str} | {proj_esc} | {desc_esc}\n")
                    elif e['write_as'] == 'running_preserve_changed':
                        # change command with new values preserving raw input spaces
                        start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
                        proj_esc = escape_str(e['project_raw_input'])
                        desc_esc = escape_str(e['description_raw_input'])
                        f.write(f"{start_str} | {proj_esc} | {desc_esc}\n")
                    else:
                        # fallback
                        pass
                else:
                    # unchanged stopped: preserve
                    # datetime_raw lstrip
                    dt_raw = e['datetime_raw'].lstrip()
                    proj_raw = e['project_raw']
                    desc_raw = e['description_raw']
                    # desc_raw rstrip trailing spaces (but keep leading)
                    # desc_raw may have trailing spaces before newline originally, we want to strip them
                    desc_rstrip = desc_raw.rstrip(" \t")
                    # Now join
                    f.write(f"{dt_raw}|{proj_raw}|{desc_rstrip}\n")

def get_now():
    return datetime.datetime.now().replace(second=0, microsecond=0)

def get_today():
    return datetime.date.today()

def parse_file_arg(args):
    # Determine file path from -f or BARTIB_FILE env
    file_opt = args.file
    if file_opt:
        return file_opt
    env_file = os.environ.get("BARTIB_FILE")
    if env_file:
        return env_file
    return None

def handle_file_not_found(filepath):
    if filepath is None:
        print("Error: Please specify a file with your activity log either as -f option or as BARTIB_FILE environment variable", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    if not os.path.exists(filepath):
        # For commands that read file (list, report, etc), original error is "Error: Could not read from file: ..."
        # For start, it creates file if not exists
        # So we need to distinguish: for start command, file creation is allowed
        # For other commands, error
        print(f"Error: Could not read from file: {filepath}\n\nCaused by:\n    No such file or directory (os error 2)", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

def load_activities_or_error(filepath, allow_missing=False):
    if filepath is None:
        print("Error: Please specify a file with your activity log either as -f option or as BARTIB_FILE environment variable", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    if not os.path.exists(filepath):
        if allow_missing:
            return [], []
        else:
            print(f"Error: Could not read from file: {filepath}\n\nCaused by:\n    No such file or directory (os error 2)", file=sys.stderr)
            sys.exit(1)
    activities, errors, err_msg = read_file(filepath)
    if err_msg:
        print(f"Error: {err_msg}", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    return activities, errors

def filter_activities(activities, args, warnings):
    # activities: list of valid only? Or all entries valid list
    # We'll work on valid_activities list (only valid)
    # Returns filtered list
    valid = [a for a in activities if a['valid']]
    # Sort by start ascending
    valid_sorted = sorted(valid, key=lambda x: x['start'])

    # Apply filters
    # Determine today, yesterday, current_week, last_week, date, from, to, project
    today = get_today()
    yesterday = today - datetime.timedelta(days=1)

    # current_week: Monday to Sunday containing today
    # Find Monday of current week
    monday_current = today - datetime.timedelta(days=today.weekday())
    sunday_current = monday_current + datetime.timedelta(days=6)
    monday_last = monday_current - datetime.timedelta(days=7)
    sunday_last = monday_current - datetime.timedelta(days=1)

    # Parse date filters with warnings
    date_filter = None
    from_filter = None
    to_filter = None

    if hasattr(args, 'date') and args.date:
        df = parse_date_with_warning(args.date, "-d/--date")
        if df is not None:
            date_filter = df

    if hasattr(args, 'from_date') and args.from_date:
        df = parse_date_with_warning(args.from_date, "--from")
        if df is not None:
            from_filter = df

    if hasattr(args, 'to_date') and args.to_date:
        df = parse_date_with_warning(args.to_date, "--to")
        if df is not None:
            to_filter = df

    # Flags
    filter_today = getattr(args, 'today', False)
    filter_yesterday = getattr(args, 'yesterday', False)
    filter_current_week = getattr(args, 'current_week', False)
    filter_last_week = getattr(args, 'last_week', False)

    filtered = valid_sorted

    if filter_today:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() == today]
    if filter_yesterday:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() == yesterday]
    if filter_current_week:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if monday_current <= a['start'].date() <= sunday_current]
    if filter_last_week:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if monday_last <= a['start'].date() <= sunday_last]
    if date_filter:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() == date_filter]
    if from_filter:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() >= from_filter]
    if to_filter:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['start'].date() <= to_filter]
    if hasattr(args, 'project') and args.project:
        filtered = [a for a in filtered if a['project'] == args.project]

    return filtered

def apply_rounding(activities, round_arg, warnings):
    if not round_arg:
        return activities, None
    round_delta = parse_round_str(round_arg)
    if round_delta is None:
        print(f'Can not parse "{round_arg}" as duration. Argument for --round is ignored')
        return activities, None
    # Round each activity's start and end (if end exists, else now)
    # For running activities, end is None, so we round start and also effective end (now) for duration calculation, but we should not modify now? We'll round start and end for display purposes only, not change actual stored.
    # So we need to return new list with rounded start/end for display
    rounded = []
    for a in activities:
        new_a = a.copy()
        new_a['original_start'] = a['start']
        new_a['original_end'] = a['end']
        new_a['start'] = round_datetime(a['start'], round_delta)
        if a['end']:
            new_a['end'] = round_datetime(a['end'], round_delta)
        else:
            # for running, end is now, rounded?
            now = get_now()
            new_a['end'] = round_datetime(now, round_delta)
        rounded.append(new_a)
    return rounded, round_delta

def compute_duration(activity, now=None, rounded=False):
    # activity has start and end (end may be None meaning running)
    # If running, end = now
    if now is None:
        now = get_now()
    start = activity['start']
    end = activity['end'] if activity['end'] else now
    # If rounded, we already rounded start and end
    delta = end - start
    return delta.total_seconds()

def format_duration_for_display(seconds):
    return format_duration(seconds)

    else:

    # We'll build list of entries in original order, but with running that are stopped modified

    for entry in activities_all:
        if not entry['valid']:

                # running -> will be stopped at start_time
                # Create new stopped entry from this running
                # Use trimmed project/description (as observed)
                # The stopped entry's start is original start, end is start_time
                stopped_entry = {
                    'valid': True,
                    'raw_line': '', # not used
                    'line_num': entry['line_num'],
                    'start': entry['start'],
                    'end': start_time,
                    'project': entry['project'], # trimmed already
                    'description': entry['description'],
                    'project_raw': entry['project_raw'],
                    'description_raw': entry['description_raw'],
                    'datetime_raw': entry['datetime_raw'],
                    'is_running': False,
                    'write_as': 'stopped_trimmed',
                }
                new_entries.append(stopped_entry)
                print(f"Stopped activity: \"{entry['description']}\" ({entry['project']}) started at {entry['start'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')} ({format_duration_for_display((start_time - entry['start']).total_seconds())})")
            else:
                # stopped remains, preserve with our preservation rules
                # We'll keep entry as is, but for writing we use special handling that preserves raw
                # For unchanged stopped, we want to write as preserved: we will keep original raw fields
                # So we keep entry unchanged, but mark for preservation

    # Now add new running activity

    }

    new_entries.append(new_running)

    # Write file
    # We need to handle preservation of old stopped: our write_file currently handles valid unchanged as preserved, but we changed running to stopped_trimmed entries which will be written as stopped_trimmed
    # For unchanged stopped entries, we need to ensure write_file preserves as per rules
    # Let's implement write_file here directly

    with open(filepath, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        for e in new_entries:

                if e.get('write_as') == 'stopped_trimmed':
                    start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

                elif e.get('write_as') == 'running_new':
                    start_str = e['start'].strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

                    desc_esc = escape_str(e['description_raw_input'])
                    f.write(f"{start_str} | {proj_esc} | {desc_esc}\n")
                else:
                    # unchanged stopped: preserve
                    dt_raw = e['datetime_raw'].lstrip()
                    proj_raw = e['project_raw']

        sys.exit(1)

    start_time = None
    if args.time:
        parsed = parse_time_with_warning(args.time)
        if parsed:
            h,m = parsed
            today = get_today()
            start_time = datetime.datetime.combine(today, datetime.time(h,m))
        else:
            start_time = get_now()
    else:
        start_time = get_now()

    activities_all, errors, _ = read_file(filepath)
    valid = [a for a in activities_all if a['valid']]
    # Build deduped list for continue index
    valid_sorted = sorted(valid, key=lambda x: x['start'], reverse=True)
    seen = set()
    deduped = []
    for a in valid_sorted:
        key = (a['description'], a['project'])
        if key not in seen:
            seen.add(key)
            deduped.append(a)

    if not deduped:
        print("Error: No activity has been started before.", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    num = 0
    if args.number is not None:
        try:
            num = int(args.number)
        except:
            num = 0
    if num <0 or num >= len(deduped):
        print(f"Error: Less than {num} distinct activities have been logged yet", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    selected = deduped[num]

    proj_input = args.project if args.project is not None else selected['project']
    desc_input = args.description if args.description is not None else selected['description']

    # Now stop running activities at start_time
    running = [a for a in valid if a['end'] is None]

    for entry in activities_all:

            new_entries.append(entry)

                    'valid': True,
                    'line_num': entry['line_num'],
                    'start': entry['start'],
                    'end': start_time,
                    'project': entry['project'],
                    'description': entry['description'],
                    'write_as': 'stopped_trimmed',

                print(f"Stopped activity: \"{entry['description']}\" ({entry['project']}) started at {entry['start'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')} ({format_duration_for_display((start_time - entry['start']).total_seconds())})")

                new_entries.append(entry)

        'description_raw_input': desc_input,

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="bartib", description="A simple timetracker")
    parser.add_argument("-f", dest="file", help="the file in which bartib tracks all the activities")
    parser.add_argument("-V", "--version", action="store_true", help="Prints version information")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="subcommand")

    # start
    p_start = subparsers.add_parser("start", help="starts a new activity")
    p_start.add_argument("-d", "--description", required=True, help="the description of the new activity")
    p_start.add_argument("-p", "--project", required=True, help="the project to which the new activity belongs")
    p_start.add_argument("-t", "--time", help="the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)")
    p_start.set_defaults(func=cmd_start)

    p_stop = subparsers.add_parser("stop", help="stops all currently running activities")
    p_stop.add_argument("-t", "--time", help="the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)")
    p_stop.set_defaults(func=cmd_stop)

    p_cancel = subparsers.add_parser("cancel", help="cancels all currently running activities")
    p_cancel.set_defaults(func=cmd_cancel)

    p_change = subparsers.add_parser("change", help="changes the current activity")
    p_change.add_argument("-d", "--description", help="the description of the new activity")
    p_change.add_argument("-p", "--project", help="the project to which the new activity belongs")
    p_change.add_argument("-t", "--time", help="the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)")
    p_change.set_defaults(func=cmd_change)

    p_continue = subparsers.add_parser("continue", help="continues a previous activity")
    p_continue.add_argument("number", nargs="?", default="0", help="the number of the activity to continue (see subcommand `last`)")
    p_continue.add_argument("-d", "--description", help="the description of the new activity")
    p_continue.add_argument("-p", "--project", help="the project to which the new activity belongs")
    p_continue.add_argument("-t", "--time", help="the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)")
    p_continue.set_defaults(func=cmd_continue)

    p_current = subparsers.add_parser("current", help="lists all currently running activities")
    p_current.set_defaults(func=cmd_current)

    p_list = subparsers.add_parser("list", help="list recent activities")
    p_list.add_argument("--current_week", action="store_true", help="show activities of the current week")
    p_list.add_argument("--last_week", action="store_true", help="show activities of the last week")
    p_list.add_argument("--no_grouping", action="store_true", help="do not group activities by date in list")
    p_list.add_argument("--today", action="store_true", help="show activities of the current day")
    p_list.add_argument("--yesterday", action="store_true", help="show yesterdays' activities")
    p_list.add_argument("-d", "--date", help="show activities of a certain date only")
    p_list.add_argument("--from", dest="from_date", help="begin of date range (inclusive)")
    p_list.add_argument("--to", dest="to_date", help="end of date range (inclusive)")
    p_list.add_argument("-n", "--number", help="maximum number of activities to display")
    p_list.add_argument("-p", "--project", help="do list activities for this project only")
    p_list.add_argument("--round", dest="round", help="rounds the start and end time to the nearest duration. Durations can be in minutes or hours. E.g. 15m or 4h")
    p_list.set_defaults(func=cmd_list)

    p_report = subparsers.add_parser("report", help="reports duration of tracked activities")
    p_report.add_argument("--current_week", action="store_true")
    p_report.add_argument("--last_week", action="store_true")
    p_report.add_argument("--today", action="store_true")
    p_report.add_argument("--yesterday", action="store_true")
    p_report.add_argument("-d", "--date", help="show activities of a certain date only")
    p_report.add_argument("--from", dest="from_date", help="begin of date range (inclusive)")
    p_report.add_argument("--to", dest="to_date", help="end of date range (inclusive)")
    p_report.add_argument("-p", "--project", help="do report activities for this project only")
    p_report.add_argument("--round", dest="round", help="rounds the start and end time to the nearest duration. Durations can be in minutes or hours. E.g. 15m or 4h")
    p_report.set_defaults(func=cmd_report)

    p_status = subparsers.add_parser("status", help="shows current status and time reports for today, current week, and current month")
    p_status.add_argument("-p", "--project", help="show status for this project only")
    p_status.set_defaults(func=cmd_status)

    p_projects = subparsers.add_parser("projects", help="list all projects")
    p_projects.add_argument("-c", "--current", action="store_true", help="prints currently running projects only")
    p_projects.add_argument("-n", "--no-quotes", action="store_true", dest="no_quotes", help="prints projects without quotes")
    p_projects.set_defaults(func=cmd_projects)

    p_last = subparsers.add_parser("last", help="displays the descriptions and projects of recent activities")
    p_last.add_argument("-n", "--number", default=10, help="maximum number of lines to display")
    p_last.set_defaults(func=cmd_last)

    p_search = subparsers.add_parser("search", help="search for existing descriptions and projects")
    p_search.add_argument("search_term", nargs="?", default="", help="the search term")
    p_search.set_defaults(func=cmd_search)

    p_check = subparsers.add_parser("check", help="checks file and reports parsing errors")
    p_check.set_defaults(func=cmd_check)

    p_sanity = subparsers.add_parser("sanity", help="checks sanity of bartib log")
    p_sanity.set_defaults(func=cmd_sanity)

    p_edit = subparsers.add_parser("edit", help="opens the activity log in an editor")
    p_edit.add_argument("-e", dest="editor", help="the command to start your preferred text editor")
    p_edit.set_defaults(func=cmd_edit)

    args = parser.parse_args()

    if args.version:
        print(VERSION)
        sys.exit(0)

    if not args.subcommand:
        parser.print_help()
        sys.exit(0)

    # file handling for commands that need file
    # For list/report/etc, file arg parsing is inside each command

    args.func(args)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
